entities.summary:
Alemanno Adimari was a renowned Italian Catholic cardinal and archbishop who played a pivotal role in the governance of the Catholic Church during the late Middle Ages. Serving as the Bishop of Lucca from 1410 to 1422, he was instrumental in shaping the Church's policies and influence on Italian politics and society.

Adimari's legacy can be seen in his continued involvement with Pope Martin V, who sought his counsel on various matters affecting the Church's global reach. This collaboration had a lasting impact on the Church's diplomatic efforts, particularly during the tumultuous period of the Papal Schism.

The exact date of Adimari's death is not certain, but he died around September 26, 1422. His passing marked the end of an era for the Catholic Church in Italy, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continued to shape the course of Italian history.

In the years following his death, the influence of the Church on Italian politics and society only grew stronger, with Adimari's successors continuing to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries between various city-states and monarchies.
